{{resize|10pt|''Bā dàn''}} {{font|size=60%|([[Pinyin]])}} | time_zone = [[Time in Indonesia|Indonesia Western Time]] | utc_offset = +7 | time_zone_DST = | utc_offset_DST = | website = {{URL|batam.go.id}} | custom_label_sec1 = [[Human Development Index|HDI]] (2023) | custom_data_sec1 = {{increase}} 0.826 ([[List of Indonesian provinces by Human Development Index|25th]]) – very high | custom_label1_sec1 = | custom_data1_sec1 = | custom_label2_sec1 = | custom_data2_sec1 = | custom_label3_sec1 = | custom_data3_sec1 = | custom_label4_sec1 = | custom_data4_sec1 = | custom_label5_sec1 = | custom_data5_sec1 = }} '''Batam''', officially the '''City of Batam''' or '''Batam City''' ({{langx|id|Kota Batam}}, not to be confused with ''Batam Kota'', a [[kecamatan|district]] within this city), is the largest [[List of regencies and cities of Indonesia|city]] in the [[Indonesian province]] of the [[Riau Islands]]. The city of Batam includes Batam Island at {{convert|410|km2|mi2}}, as well as other major islands such as [[Rempang Island|Rempang]] at {{convert|165|km2|mi2}} and [[Galang Island|Galang]] at {{convert|80|km2|mi2}}. Together, the three-[[Barelang Bridge|interconnected]] islands of the [[Riau Archipelago]] are known as ''[[Barelang]]'' (an abbreviation of Batam–Rempang–Galang). The remaining hundreds of tiny islands are largely conservation areas, small fishing outposts, or uninhabited mangroves. Collectively, the land area of all these islands make up around {{convert|1020.28|km2|mi2}}. Batam Island is the core [[Urban area|urban]] and [[Zoning|industrial zone]], while both Rempang Island and Galang Island maintain their rural character and low-density population; they are connected to Batam Island by short bridges. [[Bulan Island|Bulang Island]] and the islands to its north lie to the west of Batam Island; while they are part of the Belakang Padang District, they are also administratively within the city. Batam City is an industrial [[boomtown]], an emerging transport hub and part of a [[free trade zone]] in the [[Indonesia–Malaysia–Singapore Growth Triangle]], located {{cvt|20|km|mi}} off [[Singapore]]'s south coast.{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1991/08/03/business/worldbusiness/IHT-in-todays-booming-asia-business-knows-no.html |title=In Today's Booming Asia, Business Knows of 1,196,396,Badan Pusat Statistik, Jakarta, 2021. making it the third largest city in the region of [[Sumatra]], after [[Medan]] and [[Palembang]].{{cite web |url=https://batamkota.bps.go.id/publication/2019/08/16/f65614b25dd96d83b713d88d/kota-batam-dalam-angka-2019.html |last= |first= |title=Kota Batam Dalam Angka 2019 |website=www.batamkota.bps.go.id |access-date=4 February 2020 |archive-date=5 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210605122845/https://batamkota.bps.go.id/publication/2019/08/16/f65614b25dd96d83b713d88d/kota-batam-dalam-angka-2019.html |url-status=live }} Islands that form part of Batam are also the closest parts of [[Indonesia]] to [[Singapore]], at a minimum distance of {{cvt|6|km|miles}} across the [[Singapore Strait]]. In clear weather and good visibility, both Batam and Singapore are visible from each other with the naked eye. Batam was the fastest-growing municipality in [[Indonesia]] during the decade prior to 2010, with a population growth rate of 11% per year;{{cite web |last=Firman |first=Tommy |url=http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2012/05/12/urbanization-and-urban-development-patterns.html |title=Urbanization and urban development patterns |website=The Jarkata Post |date=12 May 2012 |access-date=11 August 2016 |archive-date=14 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210214172727/https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2012/05/12/urbanization-and-urban-development-patterns.html |url-status=live }} however, there were setbacks during the subsequent decade. In 2017, the island suffered severe job losses; some 300,000 workers were laid off.{{cite web |url=http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2017/06/16/batam-economy-in-a-state-of-emergency-mayor-says.html |title=Batam economy in a state of emergency, mayor says |first=The Jakarta |last=Post |website=thejakartapost.com |access-date=17 June 2017 |archive-date=23 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210523123818/https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2017/06/16/batam-economy-in-a-state-of-emergency-mayor-says.html |url-status=live }} The official estimated population as of mid 2025 was 1,296,960.Badan Pusat Statistik, Jakarta, 27 February 2026, ''Kota Batam Dalam Angka 2026'' (Katalog-BPS 1102001.2171)
